study.title: Accelerating crystal structure search through active learning with neural networks for rapid relaxations
study.citation: Hessmann SSP et al. npj Computational Materials 11, 44 (2025).
study.workflow_type: Active-learning crystal structure search with ensemble force-field relaxation and DFT labelling
study.assessment_scope: Published article, Supplementary Information, data and code availability statements, linked data and code records, and released configuration files; the analysis was not rerun.

items.summary: Initial and final candidate pools, acquired training structures, DFT-validated structures, and final ensembles are deposited, and the linked DepositOnce data record identifies a CC BY 4.0 licence. Generation constraints are stated, but stable item hashes, a duplicate rule with cross-split collision rate, and shortcut or perturbation checks are not reported.
source_locations: Methods, Constraints for initial structure generation

items.summary: A 20% validation split monitors ensemble training, but the grouping strategy, split manifest, random seeds, and independent test protocol are not stated.
The five-model SO(3)-equivariant ensemble, input representation, two interaction layers, 64 features, lmax=2, and 7 angstrom cutoff are described; random seeds are not provided.

Adam optimisation, batch size 10, initial learning rate 0.0005, validation-based scheduling, loss weights, and device allocation are reported; epoch counts, precision, wall-clock uncertainty for training, and matched inference throughput are incomplete.
Random and symmetry-constrained generation, interatomic-distance and lattice constraints, pool sizes, rejection rules, clustering, machine-learning relaxation, and final DFT relaxation are specified.
source_locations: Main text, Initial structure generation through Structure relaxation
Methods, Constraints for initial structure generation

items.summary: DFT evaluations needed to recover low-energy structures, relaxation outcomes, and mean and standard deviation over three simulations per composition are reported; general validity, novelty, and diversity definitions are not part of the evaluation.
source_locations: Results, Global energy minimum and Fig. 3
Results, Multiple low-energy structures and Fig. 4

items.summary: The method is compared with random search, Bayesian optimisation, and learning-accelerated local search. The paper notes that the baselines stop once the target is found, making their evaluation counts optimistic lower bounds relative to the proposed convergence criterion.
source_locations: Results, Global energy minimum and Fig. 3

items.summary: Machine-learning relaxations are escalated to DFT under a pinned Quantum ESPRESSO, PAW, PBE, pseudopotential, cutoff, k-point, force-convergence, and timeout protocol. The study establishes low-energy structures under these settings but does not make or validate route-specific synthesizability claims.
source_locations: Methods, Reference computations and Structure relaxation

items.summary: Candidate pools, acquired labels, final ensembles, configurations, installation instructions, and code are archived, but no environment lockfile, split checksums, one-command figure rebuild, or complete determinism statement is identified.

The acquisition score combines predicted energy and maximum force magnitude, while ensemble force uncertainty determines when each machine-learning relaxation is stopped. The per-cycle DFT batch varies from 100 to 200 structures; five models supply uncertainty; stopping tracks stabilisation of the k lowest-energy clusters over a stated number of cycles and energy tolerance; and total DFT counts and three simulations per composition are reported.
source_locations: Main text, Collecting training data, Structure relaxation, and Stopping criterion
Code configuration, src/scripts/configs/main.yaml and experiment configurations

items.summary: Runtime is separated into DFT labelling, ensemble training, machine-learning relaxation, and DFT validation; device allocations and the approximately 90% CPU-core-hour contribution from DFT labelling are stated, but energy and carbon estimates, candidates per GPU-hour, and associated uncertainty are not reported.
source_locations: Supplementary Section B and Supplementary Fig. 2

items.summary: The workflow searches low-energy structures for three stated inorganic compositions and does not expose a hazardous target, autonomous execution pathway, or access mechanism that makes a governance control material to the claim. Data and code licences are assessed under D1 and R1.
source_locations: Main article, Initial structure generation, Data availability, and Code availability

items.summary: DFT labels, per-cycle batch size, ensemble size, simulation replicates, validation relaxations, and device allocation are recoverable, but are not consolidated with full candidate attrition and compute in one record.

notes: This is a disclosure audit rather than a methodological quality score. No unreported detail was inferred.
